\caption{Following experiments on $64\times64$ grids in which every interior trader kept Rule~19280, with 1,000 baseline steps and 3,000 steps of following. Followers were interior traders chosen at random. Cash is the mean over followers of each follower's final cash, after every trader sold all of its shares to the dealer, divided by its cash and shares at the quoted price when following began, minus the same mean for the same traders in the paired no-following control. Non-follower Sell is the change in the fraction of time that non-followers spent in Sell, and drawdown is the change in the maximum drawdown of the quoted price. All changes are in percentage points, with pointwise 95\% intervals from resampling whole starting markets. In A, each starting market had two random assignments of followers and advice. In the masked condition, neighbors read each follower's intention from the no-following control, and the cash difference is advice minus masked. The two endpoints fixed before these markets were simulated, cash with advice and the cash difference at dealer depth $h=100$ with technical traders held, had Bonferroni-adjusted 97.5\% intervals of [25.43, 28.06] and [22.30, 25.30]. In the no-following controls at $h=100$ with technical traders held, the same non-followers spent 24.9\% of their time in Sell. In B, the change in the final 500 steps after advice stopped exceeded 20 percentage points in 38 of 100 runs and was below 5 percentage points in 61. In C, copying repeated a randomly chosen trader's completed trade from the previous step.}
\label{tab:following}
